Managing a High-Volume Caseload: You’ll oversee approximately 150 cases, with around 50 actively in litigation each month, guiding each from intake through settlement or jury verdict.

- 

Engaging with Clients: You’ll maintain proactive and transparent communication, ensuring clients are informed and supported throughout the legal process.

-

-

Expedited Processes: Access medical records swiftly through our in-house medical records company, reducing retrieval times by an average of seven days.

- 

Financial Support: All legal expenses incurred during the life of a case are covered by the firm, allowing you to focus solely on advocacy.

title: Head of U.S. Policy
posting_excerpt:
l results open sourced. This is the quickest way to close the time needed from design to world class red teaming.

This role sits between our technical team and relevant external parties. Externally, you will give policymakers an accurate picture of what can be verified today, what could be with investment, what cannot, and what each option costs. Internally, you will take the priorities emerging in domestic frontier AI regulation and in proposals for international compute agreements and turn them into specific verifiable claims, so that our researchers know what to build and our red team knows what to attack.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Define Lucid’s theory of change for frontier AI verification in the US, and where government plays a role in this

 - Give policymakers, congressional staff, agencies and the wider governance community an accurate picture of AI verification: what is possible now, what is close, what is not, and at what cost

 - Translate policy proposals into precise verifiable claims, and work with the research and red teams to test whether current mechanisms can meet them

 - Build and own Lucid's relationships in Washington and beyond, including think tanks, standards bodies and international counterparts. Define the best ways to engage with these stakeholders and deliver on them

 - Write regularly for the above audiences, including briefings, public comments, testimony and explainers

 - Track domestic frontier AI regulation and international compute-agreement proposals

 - Build the policy function as it grows




REQUIREMENTS

 - Substantial experience in US AI or technology policy, with a record of changing outcomes rather than tracking them, whether in government, Congress, a think tank or a company's policy function

 - The ability to represent technical work accurately: either enough depth to read a verification paper or system design yourself, or a demonstrated record of getting there quickly in a new technical domain

 - Track record of writing that makes technical AI governance accessible for non-experts

 - Existing relationships across the communities working on frontier AI oversight

 - Comfort operating with limited precedent, and a preference for building structure rather than inheriting it




USEFUL, NOT REQUIRED

 - A technical background in security, cryptography, hardware or distributed systems

 - Experience with verification regimes in other domains, such as arms control or nuclear safeguards

 - Experience making technical or policy work accessible to a wide audience across press, social media, multimedia and explainers, and a habit of pitching ideas rather than waiting for a brief

 - Experience in standards bodies or multi-stakeholder governance

 - Prior experience building a policy or government-affairs team




THE FIRST 90 DAYS

 - A defined theory of change and strategy for US policy. This could involve government, but it could also focus on industry standards. The person in role would be tasked with setting the priorities.

 - A system for tracking engagement and outcomes with relevant external stakeholders




PRACTICALITIES

This role is based in Washington, D.C. Regular travel to San Francisco, London and to policy and industry events should be expected. The base salary range for this role is listed above. Compensation also includes equity.



If you think you would be right for this role but do not meet every requirement, we would still like to hear from you; tell us why.

title: Immigration Staff Attorney
posting_excerpt:
Immigration Staff Attorney

Barnes & Thornburg is seeking a highly motivated Staff Attorney for our Atlanta Office with one to three years of business immigration experience to join its growing Immigration and Global Mobility Services practice group. Under the direct supervision of the Immigration Partners, the Staff Attorney works as part of a fast-paced group, working with team members across the firm. The Staff Attorney will work with a wide range of employers sponsoring foreign national workers in a wide range of corporate and technology clients, universities, financial industry and healthcare systems. The preferred candidate will have experience working with a high volume of case types, including reviewing, drafting and overseeing cases with a team of paralegals.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

 - Must be able to exercise significant discretion, apply legal research skills, formulate legal arguments and identify appropriate case law for business immigration cases.

 - Manage large caseloads, independently manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment, review, draft, and monitor petitions.

 - Must be responsive and professional to clients, deadlines and handle extensive client contact.

 - The preferred candidate will have experience with:
   
   - PERM labor certification and recruitment,
   
   - Nonimmigrant visas including H-1B, L-1, TN and E visas,
   
   - Immigrant visas including EB-1, EB-2 and EB-3 preference categories.

 - Maintain a commitment to professionalism, customer service and teamwork philosophy with clients and internal teams.

 - Strong academic performance and excellent research, writing, analytical, and communication skills are required.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Required:

 - Juris Doctor, state license, and in good standing

 - Must have at least 1-3 years of experience preparing business immigration applications and other types of immigration matters.

 - Must have a congenial personality, excellent client interaction skills and demonstrated passion for immigration work.

 - Must have the ability to manage multiple matters simultaneously and work independently as needed.

 - Candidate must be well-organized, detail-oriented, manage time efficiently, work independently as needed, astute at identifying issues and a quick learner in a fast-paced environment.

 - Ability to prioritize workload, meet strict deadlines and to interact effectively with professionals from diverse cultural backgrounds as well as in-house counsel and H.R. professionals is a must.

 - Must be detail-oriented to ensure the highest level of accuracy and be able to multi-task.


We will not consider resumes submitted by external agencies or recruiters for this position. Recruiters and agencies will not be compensated for assisting Barnes & Thornburg LLP in recruiting for this position, regardless of whether such party has a recruiting contract with us.
